cases.summary: Rd3 opens a route for the rook through d2, so its activity can continue beyond the immediate attack. Black's pawn on e2 remains one step from promotion, in front of White's rook on e1; preserving this pawn keeps that restriction while the other piece becomes active. After Rd3, Black's rook on e8 adds support to Black's pawn on e2, which is under attack from White's rook on e1. In the Rd3 line: The recorded continuation is Kg1 Rd2. Kg1 adds no new opposing controller of d2. Rd2 uses that square with Black's rook on d2, targeting White's pawn on d4. From there the rook controls c2 and b2, extending its pressure along that rank. In the Rd3 line: The recorded continuation is Rc2 Rd1. Rc2 adds control of d2 with White's rook on c2. Rd1 continues with Black's rook on d1 instead of using d2 in this line, targeting White's pawn on d4 and White's rook on e1. The compared root choices are Bd3 and Rd3.
cases.semantic_reading: Pass: continuing d2 -> c2/b2 rook activity plus replacement e8 guard of e2 and e1 blockade; Kg1 permits Rd2 while Rc2 adds d2 control and the actual reply is Rd1 attacking e1. Rc2 is an investigated functional contrast, not claimed best defense. No forced b2 entry or win is claimed.

cases.summary: a3 adds control of b4, supporting the pawn advance to b4 and contesting entry by Black's knight on c6 and Black's knight on d5. In the a3 line: The recorded continuation is O-O b4. O-O adds no new opposing controller of b4. b4 gains space with White's pawn on b4 under that support, targeting Black's bishop on c5. In the a3 line: The recorded continuation is a5 e4. a5 adds control of b4 with Black's pawn on a5. e4 continues with White's pawn on e4 instead of using b4 in this line, targeting Black's knight on d5. The compared root choices are a3 and e4.
cases.semantic_reading: Pass: a3 supports b4 and contests entry of both black knights. O-O b4 gains space and attacks Bc5; a5 adds b4 control and the actual continuation is e4 attacking Nd5. The root PV contains a5/e4, not b4; its absence no longer prevents this question. No claim that b4 becomes illegal or that the book plan is forced.
